n: Payment text field abuse and criminal communication
ds: Free-text fields on low-value payments are used as a messaging channel to stalk, harass, threaten or coerce a victim (often in family and domestic violence, including breaches of protection orders), to make extortion threats, to signal self-harm, or to communicate about criminal activity. The money is incidental; the message is the harm.

src.t: AUSTRAC (Fintel Alliance), Financial crime guide: Preventing misuse and criminal communication through payment text fields (2021-11)

cn.rt: Everyday accounts send and receive messages through payment descriptions in app and internet banking.

rat: Real-time account-to-account payments with long free-text references sent from banking apps.

ind.n: Repeated very low-value payments to one recipient carrying messages
ind.cx: Cents or a few dollars sent repeatedly to the same person, where the description field carries the real content.
ind.fp: Test payments, games between friends, or small regular allowances.
ind.ds: A sender makes frequent payments of cents or a few dollars to the same person over days or months, where the payment appears to serve as a messaging channel rather than a transfer of value.

ind.n: Payment text contains threats, coercion, references to self-harm or coded criminal terms
ind.cx: Threatening, coercive, self-harm or coded criminal language in payment descriptions, including misspellings to fit character limits or evade term lists.
ind.fp: Jokes, song lyrics or banter between consenting parties; context matters.
ind.ds: Free-text descriptions on payments include threats, harassment, demands for contact, references to suicide or self-harm, or slang, emojis and abbreviations that hide criminal meaning.

ind.n: One-sided payment messaging that continues without reply or after warnings
ind.cx: Messages flow one way only, or continue or rise in value after the sender is warned or blocked.
ind.fp: Regular one-way payments such as pocket money or rent with routine references.
ind.ds: One person keeps sending low-value payments with text to another who never replies, or the pattern resumes or escalates in value after the institution has warned or blocked the sender.

ctl.ds: Screens payment instructions, references and narrative fields for restricted parties, goods, places and concealment language using tuned matching logic. It catches exposure that does not appear in the customer record.

Provides discreet escalation routes and private conversation procedures so staff can refer suspected victims of exploitation, coercion or trafficking to specialists, police and support organisations. It prioritises victim safety.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.
